ui.tagline: The all-round Studio — image and video models, content tools, and code.
ui.description: The general-purpose workspace most bots should use. Includes Claude Code, AI Gen, the Skills CLI, a TypeScript toolchain, and all three Node package managers. Pick this when you don't need anything beyond standard web/Node/AI tooling.

@anthropic-ai/claude-code.blurb: Anthropic's coding assistant runs right inside the workspace.

packs.description: Python 3 + pip + venv + build tooling for native extensions.
packs.agentGuidance: Python 3 is at `python3` (no unversioned `python`). Use `pip3 install --break-system-packages <pkg>` for system-wide installs (this image follows PEP 668), or `python3 -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate` for a project-local venv. Native-extension build tools (build-essential, pkg-config, python3-dev) are present, so packages like Pillow, lxml, manim can compile from source if needed.

packs.description: FFmpeg for video/audio encoding and frame-to-MP4 assembly.
packs.agentGuidance: Use `ffmpeg -i <input> <output>` for transcoding, `ffmpeg -framerate <fps> -i frame_%04d.png out.mp4` for frame sequences, and `ffprobe -v quiet -print_format json -show_format -show_streams <file>` to inspect media. The Debian ffmpeg build includes the common codecs (libx264, libvpx, aac); use `-c:v libx264 -pix_fmt yuv420p` for broadly-compatible MP4 output.

packs.description: TeX Live (LaTeX) + dvisvgm — needed for MathTex / Tex rendering in animation pipelines and for PDF/SVG math output.
packs.agentGuidance: Compile LaTeX with `pdflatex <file.tex>` or `latex <file.tex>`. The texlive-latex-extra, texlive-fonts-extra, texlive-latex-recommended, texlive-science and tipa packages are included — covering Manim's `MathTex`/`Tex` requirements and most paper-style documents. Use `dvisvgm <file.dvi>` to convert DVI to SVG. First invocation is slow (font cache build); subsequent calls are fast.

packs.description: Xvfb virtual framebuffer + Mesa OpenGL libs — lets headless OpenGL workloads (ManimGL, Blender headless, etc.) render without a real display.
packs.agentGuidance: Wrap OpenGL/GUI commands with `xvfb-run -a <command>` to give them a virtual display (`-a` auto-picks a free server number). For longer pipelines export a persistent display: `Xvfb :99 -screen 0 1920x1080x24 & export DISPLAY=:99`. Required for ManimGL (`manimgl`); not required for Manim CE (`manim`) which renders headlessly via Cairo.

packs.description: Manim Community Edition (manim) + ManimGL (manimlib) — the two leading Python animation engines, with their native Cairo/Pango deps.
packs.agentGuidance: Two engines coexist. Manim CE — `manim -ql <file.py> <SceneClass>` (Cairo-based, headless, default for most agents). ManimGL — `xvfb-run -a manimgl <file.py> <SceneClass>` (OpenGL; the import itself opens a display, so any `manimgl` invocation or even `import manimlib` must be wrapped in `xvfb-run -a` or run with `DISPLAY` set — the xvfb pack provides this). Python import names differ: `import manim` vs `import manimlib`. Renders land in `./media/videos/<file>/<quality>/<SceneClass>.mp4` by default; pass `--media_dir /home/user/artifacts` to redirect into the artifacts mount. Use `-ql` (480p), `-qm` (720p), `-qh` (1080p) to trade speed for quality.

packs.description: Shared system libraries required to run a headless Chrome / Chrome Headless Shell on Debian Bookworm. Installs no browser binary — downstream packs (e.g. remotion) fetch their own Chrome.
packs.agentGuidance: Provides the native shared libraries a headless Chromium needs (NSS, GBM/Mesa, ALSA, ATK + ATK-bridge, Cairo/Pango, X composite/damage/fixes/randr, CUPS, dbus). It installs NO browser binary — tools that drive headless Chrome (Remotion, Puppeteer, Playwright) must download or point at their own Chromium build; this pack only guarantees the OS-level .so dependencies resolve. If a render fails with `error while loading shared libraries: libXXX.so: cannot open shared object file`, the missing library belongs here.

packs.description: Remotion CLI (React/HTML → MP4 video rendering) with a Chrome Headless Shell pre-downloaded at build time and exposed at a fixed, world-readable path so the non-root runtime user can render offline.
packs.agentGuidance: Remotion renders React compositions to MP4 via headless Chrome. The CLI is installed globally (`remotion`). A Chrome Headless Shell is pre-downloaded to the fixed, world-readable path /opt/remotion/chrome-headless-shell (also exported as $CHROME_HEADLESS_SHELL in interactive shells), so renders work offline without the ~150MB first-run download. Remotion has NO env var for the browser path, so you MUST pass it explicitly with the literal path (env vars are not present in non-interactive `commands.run`): `remotion render <entry> <CompositionId> /home/user/artifacts/out.mp4 --browser-executable /opt/remotion/chrome-headless-shell`. Typical flow: scaffold or open a Remotion project (`package.json` with `remotion` + `src/index.ts` calling registerRoot, and a Root that registers <Composition> ids), `npm install`, then render with the flag above. Without `--browser-executable`, Remotion re-downloads Chrome into the project's node_modules/.remotion. System ffmpeg is present (the ffmpeg pack); Remotion also bundles its own. Domain knowledge lives in the `remotion-best-practices` skill (`skills add remotion-best-practices`) — 38 rule files on captions, audio, sequencing, transitions, fonts, etc.

packs.description: HeyGen HyperFrames CLI (HTML/CSS/GSAP -> deterministic MP4 via headless Chrome + ffmpeg). Requires Node 22+. Ships 0.8.61 — 53 releases on from the 0.8.8 this pack carried since 2026-08-22. `check` remains the unified verification gate (lint + headless-browser runtime/layout/motion/contrast audit in one pass). A PINNED Chrome is pre-installed and its path frozen at /etc/sl8/chrome-path (+ /opt/chrome/chrome symlink) so renders run offline with no per-run download. THE INSTALL IS CHOWNED TO `user` (1.4.0): the CLI repairs itself at runtime, and against a root-owned tree that repair half-completes and deletes the CLI — measured, see pack.ts. Local-only/keyless render core: voiceover/captions/background-removal come from AI Gen; HeyGen cloud features and @hyperframes/aws-lambda are excluded.
packs.agentGuidance: HeyGen HyperFrames renders HTML/CSS/GSAP compositions to MP4 via headless Chrome (Puppeteer beginFrame seeking) + ffmpeg. The CLI is global (`hyperframes`). Flow: `hyperframes init --non-interactive` to scaffold, edit the composition + animation tracks, verify with `hyperframes check` (the canonical gate: lint + headless-browser runtime/layout/motion/WCAG audit; exit 0 required), then `hyperframes render --output /home/user/artifacts/out.mp4 --non-interactive`. CHROME (pinned, offline): a pinned Chrome is pre-staged; its absolute path is frozen at /etc/sl8/chrome-path and as the /opt/chrome/chrome symlink. `hyperframes doctor` auto-detects it; if a command needs it explicitly, pass `--chrome "$(cat /etc/sl8/chrome-path)"`. Do NOT trigger a Puppeteer/Chrome download and do NOT rely on image ENV (E2B `commands.run` does not inherit it). GSAP: vendor GSAP into the composition — do not depend on a render-time CDN fetch (cdn.jsdelivr.net). FONTS / OFFLINE CLOSURE (the render-time network is closed; a composition that reaches for a font at compile time is the most common way to break a sandbox render): (1) strip every `` to fonts.googleapis.com / fonts.gstatic.com and every `@import` of a remote stylesheet; (2) map each family you want to one already packed in the image — list them with `fc-list : family | sort -u`; (3) declare it with `@font-face { font-family: ''; src: local(''); }` INSIDE the composition wrapper, not in a sibling stylesheet, so the compiler inlines it; (4) verify by running the compile and confirming zero outbound font fetches, then `hyperframes check` exit 0. Never let the compiler resolve a family by name alone and never rely on a network retry — 0.8.x surfaces that failure as FONT_FETCH_UNAVAILABLE, which in a closed sandbox means a failed render, not a slow one. MEDIA (voiceover/captions/background-removal are NOT local — use AI Gen, keyless via the SL8 proxy): voiceover → `ai-gen audio tts "" -m fal-ai/kokoro/american-english`; captions/timing → `ai-gen transcribe

packs.description: Curated font set for caption/composition rendering: DejaVu family (Sans, Sans Oblique, Serif Italic at guaranteed paths) + Comic Neue (OFL casual), plus an embeddable OFL webfont pack (Inter, Outfit, Fraunces, Anton, Space Grotesk) for legible, consistent HyperFrames/video compositions. fontconfig (fc-list/fc-match) for discovery.
packs.agentGuidance: Fonts are pre-installed — do NOT probe the filesystem or fetch fonts at runtime. Guaranteed TTF paths for ffmpeg drawtext fontfile=: /usr/share/fonts/truetype/dejavu/DejaVuSans.ttf (clean sans, default), /usr/share/fonts/truetype/dejavu/DejaVuSans-Oblique.ttf (sans oblique), /usr/share/fonts/truetype/dejavu/DejaVuSerif-Italic.ttf (serif italic). Casual/handwriting: Comic Neue (OFL; resolve with `fc-match -f '%{file}' 'Comic Neue'`). Embeddable webfonts for compositions (HyperFrames HTML/CSS or ffmpeg drawtext font='...'): Inter, Outfit, Fraunces, Anton, Space Grotesk — installed under /usr/share/fonts/truetype/sl8-webfonts and registered with fontconfig, so reference by family name (e.g. `font='Inter'`) or resolve a file with `fc-match -f '%{file}' 'Outfit'`. `fc-list` enumerates everything installed. ffmpeg's drawtext is built with fontconfig, so family names work as an alternative to fontfile=.

ui.tagline: Adds Python, Manim, Remotion, HyperFrames, ffmpeg, and LaTeX on top of General.
ui.description: Everything in General, plus a full code-to-video stack: Python 3.11, Manim Community Edition + ManimGL, Remotion (React/HTML → MP4), HeyGen HyperFrames (HTML/CSS → MP4), ffmpeg, TeX Live, and Xvfb for headless GL rendering. Runs on Node 22. Use this when your bot needs to render math/diagram animations or programmatic web video.

manim.blurb: Render math and diagram animations as MP4.

remotion.blurb: Render React/HTML compositions to MP4 (Chrome Headless Shell pre-installed).

hyperframes.blurb: HeyGen HyperFrames — render HTML/CSS/GSAP compositions to MP4 (pinned Chrome at /etc/sl8/chrome-path, Pillow; voiceover/captions/background-removal via ai-gen; Node 22).

fonts.blurb: Embeddable webfonts (Inter, Outfit, Fraunces, Anton, Space Grotesk) plus DejaVu/Comic-Neue for legible compositions.

chrome-headless.blurb: Headless-Chrome system libraries that browser-based renderers depend on.

ffmpeg.blurb: Encode and convert video and audio.

deprecation.reason: Pre-Studio kitchen-sink runtime: three unrelated toolchains (Manim, Remotion, HyperFrames) in one image and no baked skills. Studio-governed runtimes replace it per toolchain — sl8-motion / sl8-motion-core cover HyperFrames.

packs.description: The machine's own operating contract, baked into /home/user: AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md, rendered from the studio record for this exact template version (R42). The copy is written by studio/scripts/build.js beside the version's template.ts while the version is cut but not yet built, and this pack refuses to build a copy rendered for any other version or any other package pins. It bakes NO .sl8/studio.json: production's launcher replaces the two contract files on every launch but never touches .sl8/, so a baked spend ceiling of 0 would outlive the contract and stop a legacy bot from spending (2026-09-23). Run parameters arrive in .sl8/run.json at provisioning. The eval runner uploads its own copy only where the image carries none, so a run on this image proves the contract that ships.
packs.agentGuidance: This machine carries its own operating contract: /home/user/AGENTS.md (read natively by Codex and Pi) and /home/user/CLAUDE.md (which imports AGENTS.md for Claude Code). It was rendered for this exact image, so the tools and versions it lists are the ones installed. Read AGENTS.md for where work goes and what this machine can do; `sl8-agent` hands the same contract to every run, including resumes. This run's parameters — autonomy, model, what you may spend — are in .sl8/run.json when a run was provisioned; no such file means no run parameters were set.

packs.description: ImageMagick 6 (convert, identify, montage, mogrify) for raster image manipulation and animated GIF assembly from PNG frames.
packs.agentGuidance: Debian ships the ImageMagick 6.x series: the entry point is `convert` (plus `identify`, `montage`, `mogrify`) — there is NO `magick` binary, do not call it. Assemble animated GIFs from PNG frames with `convert -delay 20 -loop 0 frame-*.png out.gif` (delay is in 1/100ths of a second; -loop 0 = infinite). Inspect images with `identify <file>` (one line per GIF frame). Raster formats (PNG/JPEG/GIF/WebP) are unrestricted; the default security policy only limits ghostscript-backed coders like PDF/PS.

packs.description: Bakes the image-studio media skills into /home/user/.claude/skills (via .agents/skills): media-ai-gen (run ai-gen, house rules, manifest, gates), media-image-generation (image intent to endpoint, craft), media-photo-editing (deterministic edits), media-character-sheet (identity sheets) and media-qc (deterministic checks). Repurposed from fal's skills with recorded deltas (studio/image-studio/adaptations.md). No router and no job workflow. Closes the package index system-wide (/etc/pip.conf no-index, since 1.0.2) so a job cannot pip-install from the network. Requires a GITHUB_TOKEN build env (registry read); blanked from the image ENV after install.
packs.agentGuidance: The media skills are PRE-INSTALLED (media-ai-gen, media-image-generation, media-photo-editing, media-character-sheet, media-qc). Do NOT reinstall. Every model call goes through media-ai-gen (ai-gen), and every media-* skill follows its house rules (HR-1.0, media-ai-gen/references/house-rules.md): declare then assert, cost first, never re-fire a job, gates instead of questions, checks are scripts. There is no router: a job-specific workflow comes from the bot that runs here. Deliverables go under /home/user/artifacts/<project>/ with a manifest (media-ai-gen/scripts/manifest.mjs). Package downloads are disabled on this machine (/etc/pip.conf no-index); python-runtime's pip line does not apply here: never install tools or models at runtime; if a paid step cannot run, open the spend gate and end the job partial.

ui.tagline: Generated and edited stills — for Specialists who ship images.
ui.description: Everything in General, plus five image skills adapted from fal's: choose and prompt the image model through ai-gen, edit photos locally (grades, crops, cutouts, composites with exact text added locally), make character reference sheets, and measure every file with media-qc. Python imaging (Pillow, OpenCV, scikit-image), ImageMagick, ffmpeg and a curated font set are baked; every generation is recorded in a manifest with its credits. Pick this when a bot needs finished stills at a declared size.

imagemagick.blurb: Resize, quantise, trim, montage, and measure images — the deterministic half of the work, run locally instead of asking a model.

fonts.blurb: DejaVu + Comic Neue + embeddable webfonts (Inter, Outfit, Fraunces, Anton, Space Grotesk) at known paths.

python-runtime.blurb: Python 3.11 with pip and venv for measurement scripts and JSON work.

python-imaging.blurb: Pillow, numpy, OpenCV, scikit-image, HEIC and RAW readers, pinned — for local photo work with no runtime installs.

media-image-suite.blurb: Five image skills from fal, adapted with recorded changes: generation, photo editing, character sheets, the ai-gen runner and media-qc.

The hyperframes CLI npx cache is pre-warmed: render via the project-pinned form (`npx --yes hyperframes@<pinned> render ...`). packs.description: Python 3 + pip + venv + build tooling for native extensions.
packs.agentGuidance: Python 3 is at `python3` (no unversioned `python`). Use `pip3 install --break-system-packages <pkg>` for system-wide installs (this image follows PEP 668), or `python3 -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate` for a project-local venv. packs.description: FFmpeg for video/audio encoding and frame-to-MP4 assembly.
packs.agentGuidance: Use `ffmpeg -i <input> <output>` for transcoding, `ffmpeg -framerate <fps> -i frame_%04d.png out.mp4` for frame sequences, and `ffprobe -v quiet -print_format json -show_format -show_streams <file>` to inspect media. The Debian ffmpeg build includes the common codecs (libx264, libvpx, aac); use `-c:v libx264 -pix_fmt yuv420p` for broadly-compatible MP4 output.

packs.description: Curated font set for caption/composition rendering: DejaVu family (Sans, Sans Oblique, Serif Italic at guaranteed paths) + Comic Neue (OFL casual), plus an embeddable OFL webfont pack (Inter, Outfit, Fraunces, Anton, Space Grotesk) for legible, consistent HyperFrames/video compositions. fontconfig (fc-list/fc-match) for discovery.
packs.agentGuidance: Fonts are pre-installed — do NOT probe the filesystem or fetch fonts at runtime. Guaranteed TTF paths for ffmpeg drawtext fontfile=: /usr/share/fonts/truetype/dejavu/DejaVuSans.ttf (clean sans, default), /usr/share/fonts/truetype/dejavu/DejaVuSans-Oblique.ttf (sans oblique), /usr/share/fonts/truetype/dejavu/DejaVuSerif-Italic.ttf (serif italic). Casual/handwriting: Comic Neue (OFL; resolve with `fc-match -f '%{file}' 'Comic Neue'`). Embeddable webfonts for compositions (HyperFrames HTML/CSS or ffmpeg drawtext font='...'): Inter, Outfit, Fraunces, Anton, Space Grotesk — installed under /usr/share/fonts/truetype/sl8-webfonts and registered with fontconfig, so reference by family name (e.g. `font='Inter'`) or resolve a file with `fc-match -f '%{file}' 'Outfit'`. `fc-list` enumerates everything installed. ffmpeg's drawtext is built with fontconfig, so family names work as an alternative to fontfile=.

packs.description: Shared system libraries required to run a headless Chrome / Chrome Headless Shell on Debian Bookworm. Installs no browser binary — downstream packs (e.g. remotion) fetch their own Chrome.
packs.agentGuidance: Provides the native shared libraries a headless Chromium needs (NSS, GBM/Mesa, ALSA, ATK + ATK-bridge, Cairo/Pango, X composite/damage/fixes/randr, CUPS, dbus). packs.description: HeyGen HyperFrames CLI (HTML/CSS/GSAP -> deterministic MP4 via headless Chrome + ffmpeg). Requires Node 22+. Ships 0.8.61 — 53 releases on from the 0.8.8 this pack carried since 2026-08-22. `check` remains the unified verification gate (lint + headless-browser runtime/layout/motion/contrast audit in one pass). A PINNED Chrome is pre-installed and its path frozen at /etc/sl8/chrome-path (+ /opt/chrome/chrome symlink) so renders run offline with no per-run download. THE INSTALL IS CHOWNED TO `user` (1.4.0): the CLI repairs itself at runtime, and against a root-owned tree that repair half-completes and deletes the CLI — measured, see pack.ts. Local-only/keyless render core: voiceover/captions/background-removal come from AI Gen; HeyGen cloud features and @hyperframes/aws-lambda are excluded.
packs.agentGuidance: HeyGen HyperFrames renders HTML/CSS/GSAP compositions to MP4 via headless Chrome (Puppeteer beginFrame seeking) + ffmpeg. The CLI is global (`hyperframes`). Flow: `hyperframes init --non-interactive` to scaffold, edit the composition + animation tracks, verify with `hyperframes check` (the canonical gate: lint + headless-browser runtime/layout/motion/WCAG audit; exit 0 required), then `hyperframes render --output /home/user/artifacts/out.mp4 --non-interactive`. CHROME (pinned, offline): a pinned Chrome is pre-staged; its absolute path is frozen at /etc/sl8/chrome-path and as the /opt/chrome/chrome symlink. `hyperframes doctor` auto-detects it; if a command needs it explicitly, pass `--chrome "$(cat /etc/sl8/chrome-path)"`. Do NOT trigger a Puppeteer/Chrome download and do NOT rely on image ENV (E2B `commands.run` does not inherit it). GSAP: vendor GSAP into the composition — do not depend on a render-time CDN fetch (cdn.jsdelivr.net). FONTS / OFFLINE CLOSURE (the render-time network is closed; a composition that reaches for a font at compile time is the most common way to break a sandbox render): (1) strip every `` to fonts.googleapis.com / fonts.gstatic.com and every `@import` of a remote stylesheet; (2) map each family you want to one already packed in the image — list them with `fc-list : family | sort -u`; (3) declare it with `@font-face { font-family: ''; src: local(''); }` INSIDE the composition wrapper, not in a sibling stylesheet, so the compiler inlines it; (4) verify by running the compile and confirming zero outbound font fetches, then `hyperframes check` exit 0. Never let the compiler resolve a family by name alone and never rely on a network retry — 0.8.x surfaces that failure as FONT_FETCH_UNAVAILABLE, which in a closed sandbox means a failed render, not a slow one. MEDIA (voiceover/captions/background-removal are NOT local — use AI Gen, keyless via the SL8 proxy): voiceover → `ai-gen audio tts "" -m fal-ai/kokoro/american-english`; captions/timing → `ai-gen transcribe

It installs no skill sl8-image bakes: the Image five (media-qc 1.1.0, media-ai-gen 1.0.3, media-image-generation 1.0.2 and the others) are inherited from sl8-image 1.0.1 unchanged. Repurposed from fal's skills with recorded deltas (studio/video-studio/adaptations.md). No router and no job workflow. Applied only FROM sl8-image (it needs the imaging stack, ffmpeg and fonts that sl8-image bakes). Requires a GITHUB_TOKEN build env (registry read); blanked from the image ENV after install. Package downloads stay disabled by the /etc/pip.conf (no-index) that sl8-image 1.0.1's media-image-suite 1.0.2 writes (house rule HR21).
packs.agentGuidance: The media skills are PRE-INSTALLED, twelve in all: the Image five (media-ai-gen, media-image-generation, media-photo-editing, media-character-sheet, media-qc) and the Video seven (media-video-generation, media-audio-generation, media-shot-craft, media-script-writer, media-video-production, media-motion-graphics, media-h3-prompter). Do NOT reinstall or update them. A multi-shot video from a brief starts at media-video-production, which plans it in artifacts/<project>/plan.json and hands each stage to the others; one clip starts at media-video-generation. Every model call goes through media-ai-gen (ai-gen), and every media-* skill follows its house rules (HR-1.0, media-ai-gen/references/house-rules.md): declare then assert, cost first, never re-fire a job, gates instead of questions (a spend gate stops the job partial; the next job runs gate.mjs status and resumes), checks are scripts (media-qc/scripts/mediaqc.mjs measures streams, loudness, the duck and motion as well as images). Text, titles and end cards are drawn locally by media-motion-graphics (Pillow, then one ffmpeg encode), never generated. The local tools come from sl8-image: Pillow, numpy and OpenCV pinned (never pip install), ffmpeg and ffprobe, the fonts pack (DejaVu Sans Bold; Inter, Outfit and Space Grotesk as variable fonts) and ImageMagick 6 (convert; there is no magick). There is no router: a job-specific workflow comes from the bot that runs here. Deliverables go under /home/user/artifacts/<project>/ with a manifest (media-ai-gen/scripts/manifest.mjs). Package downloads are disabled on this machine (/etc/pip.conf no-index): never install tools or models at runtime; if a paid step cannot run, open the spend gate and end the job partial.
